nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives growth in forest canopy and lake algae alike; short northern winter days slow it.

nodes.name: Lakes, ponds & wetlands
nodes.desc: Thousands of lakes and ponds and a huge network of streams make water central to life in the park.

nodes.name: Snow & winter cold
nodes.desc: Long cold winters bury forage, so winter food and shelter shape which animals thrive.

nodes.name: Forest soil & nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients in thin forest and wetland soils are cycled mainly by decomposers.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Balsam fir
nodes.desc: A common evergreen of the northern forest; its twigs and needles feed browsers in winter.

nodes.name: American beech
nodes.desc: A hardwood whose nuts are food for birds and mammals; GloBI records link it to several eaters.

nodes.name: Striped maple
nodes.desc: A small understory maple; Wikipedia lists striped maple among the new growth moose prefer.

nodes.name: Pond lilies
nodes.desc: Floating-leaved aquatic plants of ponds and slow water, a food for moose and beavers.

nodes.name: Freshwater algae
nodes.desc: Microscopic plant-like growth in lakes and streams that feeds aquatic insects.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: A big browser of new tree growth and water plants; aquatic plants supply sodium that land plants lack.

nodes.name: North American beaver
nodes.desc: Nearly wiped out by 1893 in the Adirondacks, then returned; it dams streams and creates ponds.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: Browses twigs and eats beechnuts; a main prey and carrion source for predators.

nodes.name: North American porcupine
nodes.desc: A slow bark and bud eater of the forest; the fisher is one of the few animals that regularly kills it.

nodes.name: Snowshoe hare
nodes.desc: Feeds on twigs and buds in winter; the fisher's main prey.

nodes.name: Mayflies
nodes.desc: Aquatic larvae graze algae in streams and lakes, then emerge as adults that fish and birds eat.

nodes.name: Yellow perch
nodes.desc: A common lake fish that eats insects and small prey and is food for loons.

nodes.name: Common loon
nodes.desc: Dives for fish in clear lakes; mercury that builds up in acidic lakes is a risk at the top of this chain.

nodes.name: Fisher
nodes.desc: Hunts snowshoe hares and porcupines and sometimes eats deer carrion.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever scavenger that feeds on carrion and takes other small prey.

nodes.name: Eastern coyote
nodes.desc: An opportunist: in this region deer are a main winter food, mostly scavenged, and fawns are taken in spring.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: A solitary cat of the northern forest that hunts hares and deer.
